51329239.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to IDH1 (unknown origin) by surface plasmon resonance assay

original_paragraph.SPR Analysis: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) was used to measure the binding affinity of Licochalcone A to R132H/C mutant and wild-type IDH1 proteins. Licochalcone A binds to IDH1-R132H and IDH1-R132C with an equilibrium dissociation constant Kd of 12.81 μM and 2.81 μM (Fig. 1E and F) respectively, while the Kd value for wild-type IDH1 was significantly higher (> 50 μM) (Fig. 1D). These binding results are consistent with the enzymatic results, suggesting that Licochalcone A is a selective inhibitor against the R132C mutant IDH1. In addition, mass spectrometry results showed that Licochalcone A specifically binds with R132C mutant IDH1 protein. A significant binding was observed for Licochalcone A with R132C mutant IDH1 protein, while no detectable binding was observed for Licochalcone A with R132H mutant IDH1 protein, demonstrating that Licochalcone A efficiently binds with R132C mutant IDH1 protein (Supplementary Fig. S2).
original_paragraph.Figure 1 caption: Fig. 1. Discovery of Licochalcone A as selective R132C-mutant IDH1 inhibitor, through enzymatic assay and surface plasmon resonance binding assay. Inhibitory activities of 26 natural products were determined by both wild-type and mutant IDH1 enzymatic assays. These compounds were previously reported to be active against the proliferation of sarcoma cells (A) IDH1 WT, (B) IDH1-R132H, (C) IDH1-R132C. Revealed by surface plasmon resonance, the binding of Licochalcone A with R132C-mutant IDH1 protein was more potent than its binding with wild-type or R132H-mutant IDH1 protein (D) IDH1 WT, (E) IDH1-R132H, (F) IDH1-R132C. (Error bar are mean ± S.D. for three replicates).

51329240.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to IDH1 R132C mutant (unknown origin) by surface plasmon resonance assay
51329240.references_previous: Mingay M, Chaturvedi A, Bilenky M, et al. Vitamin C-induced epigenomic re-modelling in IDH1 mutant acute myeloid leukaemia. Leukemia. 2018;32(1):11–20.

original_paragraph.SPR Analysis: To confirm the anti-tumor efficacy of Licochalcone A, the sarcoma HT-1080 cell line harboring IDH1-R132C mutation was chosen to evaluate the inhibition of Licochalcone A against cell proliferation. Suppression of HT-1080 cell proliferation was observed dose-dependently after 48 h treatment with Licochalcone A. The compound could inhibit HT-1080 cells growth with an IC50 value of 10.75 μM (Fig. 3A). We also found that the compound exhibited minimal effects against the proliferation of normal human cells RCTEC (human renal cortical tubule epithelial cells) and U-87 MG cell line containing wild-type IDH1 (IC50 > 50 μM) (Fig. 3C), demonstrating the high selectivity and low toxicity of Licochalcone A at the cellular level. HT-1080 cells usually produce high level of 2-HG due to the neomorphic enzyme function of the missense mutation in IDH1, which can be used as an indicator of cell viability. The 2-HG assay was carried out with different concentration (2 μM, 4 μM, 8 μM, 16 μM, 32 μM) of Licochalcone A. After 48 h of treatment, 2-HG levels in cells treated with different concentrations of Licochalcone A declined to less than half of the level in DMSO control, in a dose-dependent manner (Fig. 3B). Using quantitative real-time PCR analysis, the effect of Licochalcone A on CDK1 and CDK2 levels was examined.19 Treatment with Licochalcone A for 48 h led to obvious decrease for the expression of these two genes in HT-1080 cells, in a dose-dependent manner (Fig. 3D). Consistent with these findings, Licochalcone A could decrease the protein levels of CDK1 and CDK2 in HT-1080 cells in a dose-dependent manner, as compared to the DMSO control (Fig. 3E).
